newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Barlow shares dip after results disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Barlow shares dip after results disappoint.

text.p: Shares in South African industrial holding firm Barlow Ltd dipped after the firm posted half year results below analysts' expectations, dealers said on Monday.
The firm's share was down 50 cents to 48.90 rand at 1240 GMT after the group posted an interim earnings per share of 145.4 cents, below the bottom end of analysts' expectations.
"The results are not good. It looks like the share could slide down a bit further," one dealer commented.
Barlow's figures come hot on the heels of a raft of poor corporate earnings data in recent weeks that have blighted the short-term outlook for the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
The rot started with leading retailer Edgars Ltd who reported a drop in year earnings to 598 cents per share from 642 cents, disappointing analysts who reached a consensus forecast of 638 cents.
Since Edgars, more disappointing results and profit warnings followed from key industrial and retail companies, including packaging company Nampak and cement company PPC Ltd.
